chunks.text: If you want to become a machine learning engineer, then there are 9 important skills that you have to master.
Let's talk about them one by one.
Now, machine learning includes making such models that are learned from data so that you can make a pre-evaluation or decision.
As a machine learning engineer, you have to be able to deploy the model from programming and mathematics in various skills.
First of all, you have to be a part of Python.
This is the main language used in machine learning.
It is very simple and you can understand it in 1 or 2 months.
Now, some job-seekers can demand other languages like Java, R or C++, but just pay attention to Python as a beginner.
Try to learn everything together and don't bother yourself.
First, get the Python skill.
The next thing you have to learn is a version control system like Git.
Git is not a programming language.
It is a tool that we use to track changes in our code and to cooperate with others.
There are many features in Git, but you don't need to learn them all.
Try to understand it as 80-20 rules.
You use 20% of the Git's time, so 1-2 weeks of practice is enough.
You have to go deep into data structures and algorithms.
I know that many self-taught engineers leave this step, but believe me, it is very important.
First of all, understanding these examples will really improve your problem-solving skills, which are important to deal with difficult challenges.
And big tech companies like Google, Amazon and Facebook like to know about data structure and algorithm in job-seekers.
Also, by using the right data structures, you can properly organize large data sets and run your algorithm smoothly.
Spend 1-2 months on it and you will be in a good state.
You will have to be easy with SQL. SQL means Structured Query Language.
This is a very simple language that we use to work with the database.
As a machine learning engineer, you should know how to use SQL to access and organize the necessary data for your model.
SQL is very simple and you can understand it in about 1-2 months.
By the way, I have made a free PDF for you to help you in this journey, which breaks down the special insights you need to learn for each skill.
This is a great resource for your progress, to find the difference in your knowledge and to prepare for the test.
You will find the link in the description box.
Also, if you want a well-developed education, I have a full course on this channel on many tutorials and my website.
Again, the link is in the description box.
The next thing you need is a strong foundation in mathematics and computer science.
This is important because machine learning algorithms are based on these principles.
Pay attention to linear algebra, calculus, algebra and mathematics.
These will help you understand how machine learning algorithms work and how to optimize them.
It takes about 2-3 months to get a skill in these subjects.
After that, you will have to be an expert in making and visualizing data for your models.
This means cleaning the data and arranging it in such a way that your model can easily understand it.
You will have to learn to use tools like pandas and numpy to manipulate and clean the data.
Once your data is cleared, you will have to visualize it to understand the pattern and to visualize the results.
Python libraries like matplotlib and cbon will help you to make a comprehensive visualization to identify trends and vulnerabilities.
If your Python and SQL have a strong foundation, then you can understand data pre-processing and visualization in 1-2 months.
Now let's talk about the basic principles of machine learning.
Machine learning algorithms come in two strains, the approximate and the acquired.
In approximate training, you learn from model label data.
This means that a random output comes with every input.
In unsupervised learning, the model works with data without label and tries to identify patterns and relations.
It is important to learn about these algorithms and their way of working.
You will have to be familiar with things like tensorflow, pytorch and scikit-learn.
These are necessary tools to use to make and train machine learning models.
You will have to spend 3-4 months to use these tools effectively.
Once you understand the basics, you will have time to delve into advanced machine learning.
It includes the technique of ensemble learning, which combines many models for improvement in presentation, and deep learning,
which includes many layers of neural networks.
You will have to learn about natural language processing or NLP, which works with text data and computer vision, which works with images.
These advanced subjects will help you solve more complex problems and make more sophisticated models.
Spend 2-3 months on these advanced concepts so that you can deepen your knowledge and skills.
Finally, you need to know how to use the models you make.
This means that you learn to make simple web services that allow other applications to use your model.
You can do this by learning Python frameworks like Flask or Django.
You should also learn about Docker, which is a tool that makes it easy to package your model and all its components so that it runs easily on any machine.
Consider it as if everything you need to run your model is packed in a box so that it runs anywhere.
Spend 1-2 months to get the skills you need to use these basic things so that you can make your models self-confident and make them available to the real world.
If you are dedicated 3-5 hours every day, then you can follow this roadmap and get all the skills for entry-level machine learning jobs in about 12-20 months.

I will try to answer you in this video or in my future videos.
If you liked this video, please like it and subscribe for more useful content.
